newsitem.title: UK: AC-Milan float plans yet to be finalised - adviser.
newsitem.headline: AC-Milan float plans yet to be finalised - adviser.

text.p: Italian soccer champions AC Milan are considering a stock market flotation but have yet to decide on any of the details of the listing, one of their senior finanical advisers said on Tuesday.
"They have not decided how and when they will float and they have not decided where. We are still at an early stage," Stefano Marsaglia, chief executive of Rothschild Italia, told Reuters.
A report in the Guardian newspaper on Tuesday said that Milan were seeking to list in London next year in a 500 million pound flotation.

Marsaglia said that Rothschild had carried out a business review on behalf of Milan, the club owned by media magnate and former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, and outlined various ways the club could come to the market.
The club was now examining its options, Marsaglia said. He added that the 500 million pound tag was "the newspaper's figure not ours".
Marsaglia said that Milan, like English champions Manchester United, appealed to a global audience but it would take time for Milan to build up its commercial activities.
The Manchester club joined the stock market more than five years ago and is now valued at over 400 million pounds.

A number of Italian clubs are considering flotations but the situation is complicated by the fact that a company must be able to boast three straight years of profit before it is admitted to the Milan exchange.
Italian clubs have long been bankrolled by their wealthy industrialist owners and few are profitable in their own right.
